item.title: How Dolly Parton wrote the story of a changing America
item.description:
Dolly Parton was just 5-foot-nothing tall. She needed platform heels to make her feel that she could fill a performance space. Her husband, Carl Dean, once told her that from the audience, her platinum wigs made her tiny figure look like a Q-tip. But no amount of mocking could make her surrender the hair, heels, and rhinestones, which were her own brand of feminism under wraps. “Believe it or not, I had to fight for that look!” she wrote in her 2023 memoir, Behind the Seams . The look wasn’t about showbiz. It was about sovereignty. And it must have been more than passingly rewarding for Parton to know that her audience finally understood this about her before she died, at the age of 80—to know that she was fully appreciated for the wallop of woman she was. item.title: Jed York’s trailer park arrest exposed inequality in America | Lee Escobedo
item.description:
The San Francisco 49ers owner’s arrest in Ohio over the weekend was quickly put behind him. Others are not so lucky The Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community sits off state Route 170, on the edge of East Palestine, Ohio, a town most Americans only learned about because a train derailed there in February 2023 and released toxic chemicals into the creek . I grew up in a trailer park like this one, and know the sights. The grid of aluminum boxes in rows. Skirting the color of old teeth, some of it buckled, some patched with a piece of lattice.
